hypotheses.claim: A removal priority of the form score_i = removal_savings_i/scale * (1 + beta*route_load_frac_i^2) * (1 + gamma*route_dist_share_i) with scale = mean(d(0,1..n)) keeps the hook dimensionless (no O(1/s^2) scale collapse, cf. method-cvrp-frozen-c-near-tie), and biasing toward routes with load near/over capacity plus high distance share removes the customers whose reinsertion Regret-2 can actually restructure — yielding lower mean objective on dev_24 (currently 16.0201) with emphasis on the weakest regimes (capacity_level=tight, size=100, depot_style=eccentric), because tight-capacity instances are exactly where load-aware ruin selection changes the repair outcome. Stagnation gating (stagnation_ratio, iter_frac) adds deterministic pseudo-noise only when the LNS is stalling, preserving early convergence.

next_search_advice.direction: Evolve score_ruin_nodes toward a scale-normalized, capacity-and-stagnation-adaptive removal priority that targets nodes from over-full / long routes (tight-capacity regime) while decaying toward worst-cost removal when time is plentiful.
